doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Feeling out of place at a modern-leaning party
summary: At this party with contemporary players, colleagues reassure him that jazz is not a competition.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: parties I work, they don’t extend this far into more contemporary music than this party is doing. Because again, these people are very opinionated about what style of music they like. And they don’t want it to get over that way. But these guys here are extending the envelope a little bit. But it makes me feel a little bit of a fish out of water because I’m not so sure I fit in with everything that is going on. But I do my best, and I figure a lot of people seem to enjoy the way I play so I’m going to do what I do, and if you like it fine, well if you don’t like it, okay, I’m sorry, I did the best I could.
We might even have a little Latin here at this gig.
Yeah I know. Well you’ve got one of the greatest Latin players in the business, Dave Valentin. And boy what a monster he is man.

But there again all the guys, all the musicians, nobody’s out to get everybody. We’re all on everybody’s side. We had a little party of Don Miller’s last night and Dave and Charlie Sepluveda got up and played a real heavy, Latin, modern thing you know, and then Don says, “Allen, you want to come up and play?” And I’m like, “You know guys, I really don’t know any of that stuff, I just know some kind of standard tunes.” And Roland Hanna and Jay Leonhart say, “Allen, play whatever you want.” Bill Watrous, “Whatever you want, don’t worry about it, man. So you don’t have to worry about being challenged or somebody out to get you, because it’s not that way, and it shouldn’t be that way. This is not a competition. That’s my biggest problem with, you talk about jazz education people. That’s my biggest problem is they set up this thing that’s kind of a competition. There isn’t enough of us to be out to get each other. We should be on everybody else’s side.
